faq.question: What's the difference between UPC-A and EAN-13?
faq.answer: UPC-A (12 digits) is the standard in the US and Canada; EAN-13 (13 digits) is used almost everywhere else. They're not just similar — a UPC-A code is literally an EAN-13 code with an invisible leading 0, encoded with the exact same bar patterns, which is why most scanners read both without configuration.

faq.question: Is this a real, scannable barcode?
faq.answer: Yes — it's built from the same standard bar-pattern tables real scanners expect (via the same encoder as this site's EAN-13 Barcode Generator, since UPC-A and EAN-13 share identical underlying encoding), not a decorative image. Downloaded as SVG, it should scan correctly when printed at a reasonable size.
